sum: A three-week camping journey from Juphal past Phoksundo Lake, over the 5,350 m Kang La to Shey Gompa and Saldang, returning by the Jeng La and the Tarap valley.

guide.note: Upper and Lower Dolpo are restricted areas: the permits are issued only through a registered trekking agency and you must walk with a licensed guide. In practice you need a crew as well. Trails beyond the lake are unmarked, villages are a day or more apart, and river levels, snow on the passes and the condition of the pack animals decide each day's plan.

access: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, spend the night, and take the early flight to Juphal in Dolpa next morning. Juphal flights run only in calm, clear weather and are least reliable in the monsoon, which is also the best season for the trek, so allow spare days at both ends. Crews and pack animals are usually arranged to meet you in Juphal or Dunai.

photo.a: An old chorten with faded painted panels and a thatched wooden canopy stands on a bare plain, with the low houses of a village and snow-covered peaks in the distance.
photo.c: A chorten in the Tarap valley near Dho Tarap

includes: porters or pack animals and a camp crew
tents and all meals on the trek
restricted-area and Shey Phoksundo park permits in most packages (the Upper Dolpo permit alone is USD 500 for ten days, then USD 50 a day; confirm)

permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.

permits.name: Lower Dolpo restricted area permit
permits.fee: USD 20 per person per week, then USD 5 a day

fees.per: person per week, then USD 5 a day

permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.

permits.name: Shey Phoksundo National Park entry permit
permits.where: Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, or the park entry post on the trail in from Juphal.

transportText: Flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj and on to Juphal, and the same back
tips: Plan the days against the permit: the Upper Dolpo permit now costs USD 50 for each day you spend inside the restricted area, so every extra day there adds to the bill. Your agency sets the entry and exit dates.
Bring a sleeping bag rated to about minus 15 °C and a proper down jacket, even in July. Clear nights at 4,500 m freeze.
Sun and wind are fierce on the plateau. Pack a wide hat, good sunglasses, lip balm and more sunscreen than you think you need.
Carry river sandals and a small dry bag for the wading days.
Walk clockwise round Buddhist chortens and mani walls but anticlockwise round Bon ones; your guide will know which is which.

days.t: Fly to Juphal, walk to Dunai
days.note: The dawn flight from Nepalgunj, then an easy walk down to the Thuli Bheri and up the valley road to the district town. Permits are registered here and the crew makes its last purchases of fuel and fresh food.

Cross the river, follow it down to the national park gate at Suligad and turn north into the gorge. The trail rises and falls beside the water through walnut and pine. Permits are checked at the gate.
Many short climbs and descents along the river, crossing it on log and suspension bridges. Past Rechi the valley divides at Sumduwa; camp or lodge a little further on near the clinic at Chunuwar.

days.t: Chunuwar to Ringmo and Phoksundo Lake
days.note: A steady climb through Palam to the ridge where the waterfall and then the lake come into view, followed by an easy descent through birch to Ringmo on the southern shore.
The crew reorganises loads for the high country while you walk the shore to the Bon monastery at Tshowa. A second night at this height makes the days before the Kang La noticeably safer.

days.t: Along the lake to Phoksundo Khola camp
days.note: The cliff path: a narrow ledge above the western shore, in places built out on timber, that climbs to a crest at about 4,040 m before dropping to the flood plain at the head of the lake. Laden animals find it awkward, so let them go ahead.

days.t: Phoksundo Khola to Kang La base camp
days.note: Up the wide valley floor, then north-east into a tight side gorge where you wade the stream several times and clamber over boulders before it opens into high pasture. Camp below the pass. Sandals for the crossings save your boots.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 770 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.t: Over the Kang La to Shey Gompa
days.note: A steep, loose climb of three hours or more on slate scree, often with snow near the top, then a long descent beside the river to the red chortens of Shey. Start early and stay together; this is no place to be caught in afternoon cloud.

Visit the monastery if the caretaker is there and walk to Tsakang, the hermitage built into a cliff about an hour away. The full pilgrim circuit of the Crystal Mountain is a long day that climbs above 5,000 m; try it only if everyone is going well.

days.t: Shey Gompa to Namgung over the Saldang La
days.note: Follow a stony side canyon and zigzag up bare, eroded slopes to the pass, steep only near the top, then descend dry hills to Namgung, where a small red monastery stands against the wall of a gorge. Water is scarce on the climb.
A high, dusty traverse with the brown hills of Tibet to the north, then a steep drop to Saldang, the largest village of the Nangkhong valley, strung along terraces above the river.

South up the Nagon Khola through Namdo, past chortens, mani walls and fields of barley, to camp near the stone houses of Sibu. A gentle day; yak caravans share the trail in summer. Itineraries disagree about Sibu's height by several hundred metres.

Follow the river for a couple of hours, then turn up a steep side valley to pasture below the pass. Crews pitch at different heights here, which is why published altitudes for this camp run from about 4,400 to 4,900 m.

days.t: Over the Jeng La to Tokyu
days.note: About two hours of climbing to the pass, with the north side of the Dhaulagiri range on the southern skyline in clear weather, then a rough descent into the head of the Tarap valley and an easy walk down to Tokyu.
A short walk down a broad, flat valley of barley fields, passing monasteries of both the Bon and Buddhist traditions. Dho has a school, a few shops and simple places to stay, the first since Ringmo.
Wash, rest the animals and walk up to the Ribo Bumpa monastery above the village or across to the Bon monastery at Shipchok. People here are used to trekkers and may well ask you in for butter tea.

days.t: Dho Tarap to the Tarap Khola camp
days.note: Down the valley until it narrows into a gorge of juniper and wild rose, where blue sheep graze the slopes. Camp on a meadow beside the river at Kamakharka.

days.t: Tarap Khola camp to Laini Odar
days.note: The gorge at its narrowest: a path cut into cliffs, slab bridges and stretches rebuilt after each summer's floods. Camps in this section move with the state of the trail, and agencies give them different names and heights.
Out of the gorge to the junction with the Barbung Khola, then along the main valley to the old fortress village of Tarakot on its hill. The air is warm and thick again after two weeks up high.
An easy walk west beside the Thuli Bheri on a broad track, back to the bazaar, hot water and phone signal of the district town.
Down the valley and up the last climb of about 400 m to the airstrip. Many groups ride this stretch in a jeep and spend the afternoon paying off the crew.
Flights leave soon after sunrise when the weather allows. In the monsoon a wait of a day or two is common, so do not book an international flight close behind this one.
